title: Tick is built, but the live page calls it settled
text: The tick noun, the tick verb, the Tick layer and walk step 8 are marked settled, which the legend defines as “decided, not built yet”. The tick card itself says it is built (model, Rust, loops tick, --check), and Decisions says TK1 to TK13 are ruled and built and step 4 is closed. Walk step 8 still says the tick record is “proposed and not built”. The prototype marks tick proved and drops the stale sentence.

title: Grant is marked settled while IS3, IS4, IS5 and IS7 are open
text: Those four entries decide what a grant holds, how it ends and who may give one. The prototype marks grant open and links them.

title: Two definitions of proved
text: The page's legend says “a theorem in model/Laws, pinned by vectors”. words.json says “listed model laws proved under their premises; not a proof of every product surface”. The prototype uses one definition that says both.

title: Settled or planned?
text: The apply verb is settled. The lens card says emitting accepted edits “remains planned”. Those describe the same step. Which is it?

title: One word for decided
text: The grammar says settled; Decisions says ruled. The prototype keeps settled here and ruled on Decisions. One word would read more cleanly.

title: The matrix leaves out group, and the record claim doesn't hold
text: The page names thirteen verbs, and the matrix has twelve: group has no column. It also has eight of the thirteen nouns. The live caption says the record is “the one noun every verb touches”, but its row has nine of twelve cells (no tick, render or parse). The prototype says the record is touched by more verbs than any other noun.

title: The observer is the key, as built
text: The live sentence and walk write the observer as a lineage, sl:ada…, while the observer card says that today it is the signing key, k:…. The prototype writes k:rosa…, which is what is built.

title: The walk is a family recipe now
text: The live walk replays the vector 01-decision, a decision about decision:auth. You asked for something less technical, so the prototype tells the same nine steps with a recipe. The records, the heads, the counts and the tick match the vector step for step; only the words changed.

title: The walk comes before the reference now
text: The live page puts the record, then thirteen noun cards and the verbs, then the walk. The prototype tells the story first and keeps the dictionary for after, so each word has been seen in use before it is defined.

title: The order of the read path is my reading
text: The pipeline orders the read verbs as settle, admit, take, test, follow, group, fold. by.after-admission fixes where group sits; the rest is my reading of the laws. Check it.

title: The last step is a playground
text: Ben's edit plays by itself, as in the vector. After that you can type your own edit and apply it, which adds a record G that is not in the vector. It is labelled as yours.

title: The chip map became six shapes and a list
text: The live page opens with every law at once, a chip for each law on the row of the layer it governs. The prototype opens with the six shapes, each a filter, and lists all 124 sentences under the eight questions with a search. Nothing in a sentence, scope or premise was rewritten; they are copied from the built page.

title: Each law's own break card is gone
text: The live page has a Try to break it card under most questions, which varies what a law lets vary (the arrival order, a repeat) and shows the model's answer. Those cases now sit under each law on the bench, and the premise cases have their own section.

title: The bench works things out in your browser
text: The live page says nothing is computed in your browser. The bench runs a small copy of five rules here so you can change them. With the protocol's choices it gives all 71 answers the model's vectors give, checked when the page is built. Every other choice is the prototype's own, with no model behind it. Is that acceptable on the live site, or should the bench stay a prototype?

title: Which rules, and which wrong choices, are my picks
text: The five rules and the wrong choices offered for each are my reading of the laws, chosen because each one breaks a law you can see. The model doesn't list alternatives.

title: The coverage table no longer opens the page
text: The live page opens with a 124-row table, then the map, then a card for every law. The prototype opens with the chain from claim to code, lets you follow one law at a time down it, then shows the map, and ends with the gaps. Nothing on a live card is dropped: pick its law.

title: Tick says nothing is proved, but tick laws are
text: The live page lists the Tick layer as “no laws yet” and says “Nothing is built here yet, so nothing is proved.” Six tick.* laws are proved and pinned, all filed under State in laws.json. Either they belong to Tick, or the Tick note should say where they are.

title: One law at a time, in place of 124 cards
text: Each live card's rows (proved by, pinned by, run by, rests on, carries) are the steps here, in the same order and from the same joins. The live address #law-count-perm becomes #ev-count-perm, because the Laws view already uses #law-.

title: Run by now counts files
text: The live card names the implementations that run any of a law's vectors. The prototype counts how many of its files each one runs, using the live page's own rule one file at a time. That is how the tick gap shows: JavaScript runs none of them, Rust runs all of them.

title: Half the laws have two lists that differ
text: For 62 of the 124 laws, protocol/laws.md cites one set of vectors and the vectors' own laws fields name another. write.checked cites 197 files that don't name it. A file may pin a law without naming it, so this may be fine, but at this size it is the largest gap on the page. Worth closing, or worth a sentence saying why it's expected?

title: The demo column is gone
text: The live table marks the laws that have a Try to break it card. Those cases are now the bench on the Laws page, which runs a copy of five rules in your browser and is not evidence, so the gaps leave it out. A law the bench covers still links to it from its claim.

title: The map is drawn a little larger
text: The map is laid out by the live page's own code, copied with larger sizes so its labels are 12px instead of 11px. The arrangement can differ slightly from the live one; the laws and lines are the same.

title: The bookkeeping is gone from the top
text: The live page opens with which entries have left the file (PV1 to PV7, RC1, W7 …) and eight bullets about ruled work. The prototype opens with the eleven open questions and moves everything ruled into one log.

title: IS6 and IS8 name only one option
text: Both entries give a recommendation and no alternatives. The prototype writes the implied alternative beside each, marked as not argued in the entry.

title: The dependency map is my reading
text: Most edges are said in the entries (IS3 feeds IS4, IS8 and IS9; IS5 and IS8 feed IS6; IS2 and IS10 gate IS11's option B). IS7 to IS5 is my inference.
